instructions.content: Specify observable behavior, not implementation details.
Keep a shared language across product, engineering, and QA.
Scenarios should be deterministic and independently executable.
Feature files should remain readable by non-developers.
Align on examples in a Three Amigos discussion before writing scenarios.
Write scenarios in Gherkin using Given/When/Then.
Implement step definitions that map to business language.
Execute Cucumber and review failures by scenario intent.
If scenarios fail due to incorrect business logic, loop back to step 2 to clarify requirements.
If scenarios fail due to step definition errors or missing steps, loop back to step 3; run npx cucumber-js --dry-run to identify missing step definitions before full execution.
For async timing issues, verify step definitions properly await promises.
Refactor scenarios and steps to remove duplication.
Use business-facing language in feature files.
Keep each scenario focused on one behavior.
Avoid cross-scenario state coupling.
NEVER encode implementation details in Gherkin steps.
NEVER skip Three Amigos before writing key scenarios.
NEVER use vague Then steps without observable outcomes.
NEVER couple scenarios with ordering dependencies.
Prefer explicit examples over abstract wording.
Reuse step phrases only when semantics are identical.
Do not use BDD feature files for low-level unit behavior that is internal and not stakeholder-facing.
Run tagged subsets with --tags, for example "@smoke and not @wip".
Generate a JSON report with --format json:reports/cucumber-report.json for CI and reporting.
Keep the scenario count per feature manageable.
